newsitem.title: GERMANY: German analysts' comment on budget pact delay talk.
newsitem.headline: German analysts' comment on budget pact delay talk.

text.p: Following are comments from German analysts about reports from a meeting of European finance ministers in Luxembourg that France wants a period of reflection before a final agreement on the "stability pact" to ensure fiscal discipline after the launch of the euro.
THOMAS MEYER, SENIOR ECONOMIST, GOLDMAN SACHS (FRANKFURT)

"This is not necessarily contradictory. It shows in the first place that France still feels itself bound to the conditions set down for monetary union and that it still has an interest in introducing the euro on time.

"I think the French are playing for time. It would have been far more surprising if a new French government, just a week old and at its very first internationally significant meeting, were to have simply followed the footsteps of their predecessors immediately.
"It is a healthy thing to seek time, and a positive sign that they are taking time for reflection. The door is still open for an agreement.
"I think the reaction on the markets is exagerated and hasty."

"This is not a big surprise. The French are just out of an election and have not had much time to find possible lines of compromise. (Finance Minister Theo) Waigel is hardly in a mood to give in. He doesn't want to be seen coming home having given in to France."

"It may now be the end of the month, not in Amsterdam, before the stability pact can be finally approved. The time may simply be too short to get it done before Amsterdam. I would be surprised if France were trying to get a delay. They are now probing and checking their options. This is not a big blow to EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union), but adds to other concerns."
